newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech airline CSA to raise rates 3 pct on Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Czech airline CSA to raise rates 3 pct on Jan 1.

text.p: Czech airline Ceska Aerolinie (CSA) a.s. said on Monday it would raise ticket prices by an average of three percent as of January 1, to offset higher fuel costs.
The airline said in a statement that the increase would come in the form of an "extra charge", granted with the approval of the Finance Ministry.
"This extra charge will be added to the price of air tickets to at least partially cover the costs resulting from the increase in fuel prices," the statement said.
It added that fuel prices have risen by about 40 percent year-on-year.

CSA is majority-owned by the state through its agencies Konsolidcani Banka a.s. and the National Property Fund, a state privatisation agency. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (ERBD)holds a 16 percent share of CSA.
Other minor shareholders include the investment fund RIF and insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s..
